paragraphs.title: Encouragement for the Temple Builders and the Promise of Its Glory

answers: Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the residue of the people
Only the priests
Only the kings of the nations
easy.explanation: The message was given to Zerubbabel, Joshua the high priest, and the residue of the people.
easy.q: To whom did the LORD speak through Haggai?

answers: Who had seen it in its first glory
Who had built the king's palace
Who had guarded the city gate
easy.explanation: Haggai asked, “Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory?”
easy.q: What did Haggai ask about the former house?

answers: Leave the work
Wait for a king
Be strong and work
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “Be strong... and work.”
easy.q: What did the LORD command Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people to do?

answers: Take courage and continue the work
Hide from the enemy
Stop building
medium.explanation: The command is an encouragement to remain courageous and keep working.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “be strong” mean?

answers: Because the LORD promised, “I am with you”
Because the Temple was already finished
Because building was unnecessary
medium.explanation: The LORD encouraged them with the promise, “I am with you.”
medium.q: Why were the people told to be strong despite the comparison with the first Temple?

answers: It would remain without glory
It would have greater glory and peace
It would become a royal palace
medium.explanation: The LORD said the glory of the latter house would be greater and that He would give peace there.
medium.q: What would happen to the latter house according to the promise?

answers: The LORD’s presence encouraged the people to continue working
The LORD’s presence removed the need to build
The LORD’s presence was promised only to the priests
challenge.explanation: The command to work follows the promise, “I am with you.”
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the LORD’s presence and the command to build?

answers: Peace, building, and then the shaking of the nations
The shaking of the nations, the coming of the desire of all nations, and the filling of the house with glory
The filling of the house with glory, the Exodus, and then the shaking of the nations
challenge.explanation: The LORD speaks of shaking the nations, the desire of all nations coming, and filling the house with glory.
challenge.q: What sequence is described in the LORD’s promise?

answers: Its glory depends only on the people’s wealth
The silver and gold belong to the LORD, who can provide glory for the house
The house will receive no glory
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes that the LORD owns the silver and gold in connection with His promise concerning the house.
challenge.q: What does “The silver is mine, and the gold is mine” show about the Temple’s glory?

paragraphs.title: Holiness, Impurity, and the Condition of the People

answers: The priests
The kings of the nations
The farmers
easy.explanation: The LORD told Haggai to ask the priests concerning the law.
easy.q: Whom did Haggai tell the people to ask concerning the law?

answers: Yes
No
Only the wine
easy.q: Would holy flesh make bread, pottage, wine, oil, or meat holy by contact with a garment?

answers: They became unclean
They became holy
They disappeared
easy.explanation: The priests answered, “It shall be unclean.”
easy.q: What happened when an unclean person touched those things?

answers: Set apart or sacred
Broken apart
Made larger
medium.explanation: Haggai asked whether the food would become sacred through contact with holy flesh.
medium.q: What does the word “holy” mean in Haggai’s question?

answers: Holiness passed automatically, but uncleanness did not
Holiness did not pass through the contact described, but uncleanness did make things unclean
There was no distinction between holiness and uncleanness
medium.explanation: The priests answered “No” about holiness but said that uncleanness would result from the unclean person’s touch.
medium.q: What distinction appears in the priests’ answers?

answers: The people and their works were unclean before the LORD
The people were holy because of all their works
The people had no connection to the questions
medium.explanation: Haggai declared that the people, their works, and what they offered were unclean.
medium.q: How did Haggai apply the priests’ answers to the people?

answers: To show that offering something holy did not make all the people’s works clean
To prove that the priests did not know the law
To describe the amount of the harvest
challenge.explanation: Haggai used the priests’ answers to explain the spiritual condition of the people and their works.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of Haggai’s questions about holiness and uncleanness?

answers: Holiness did not pass through the described contact, but uncleanness did make things unclean
Holiness and uncleanness worked in exactly the same way
The priests answered neither question
challenge.explanation: The contrast between “No” and “It shall be unclean” is central to Haggai’s point.
challenge.q: What important contrast might be missed in the two answers?

answers: Only the holy flesh
The people, their works, and what they offered there
Only the priest’s garment
challenge.explanation: Haggai said that the people, every work of their hands, and what they offered there were unclean.
challenge.q: What did Haggai say was unclean?

paragraphs.title: Agricultural Hardship and the Turning Point to Blessing

answers: What had happened from that day and upward
Only the wars of the past
The names of the priests
easy.explanation: The people were told to consider what had happened from that day and upward.
easy.q: What did Haggai tell the people to consider?

answers: It provided twenty
It provided only ten
It provided fifty
easy.explanation: The passage says that from a heap of twenty measures there were but ten.
easy.q: What happened to the heap that was expected to provide twenty measures?

answers: Blasting, mildew, and hail
Fire, famine, and war
Wind, rain, and snow
easy.explanation: The LORD mentioned blasting, mildew, and hail.
easy.q: With what troubles did the LORD smite the people?

answers: A place for storing grain
A place of prayer
A vessel for carrying water
medium.explanation: The barn was the place where the seed or grain was stored.
medium.q: What is a “barn” in this passage?

answers: The amount received was less than expected
The amount received was doubled
The harvest was not measured
medium.explanation: Twenty measures became ten, and fifty vessels from the press became only twenty.
medium.q: What was the result of the harvest before the turning point?

answers: The LORD would bless the people
The LORD would stop speaking
The crops would disappear
medium.explanation: The LORD said, “From this day will I bless you.”
medium.q: What change was promised from the day the foundation of the LORD’s Temple was laid?

answers: The LORD smote their labours, yet they did not turn to Him
The troubles occurred only outside the land
The troubles did not affect their crops
challenge.explanation: The LORD said He had smitten all the labours of their hands, “yet ye turned not to me.”
challenge.q: How is the people’s response connected with the agricultural troubles?

answers: Blessing, the Temple’s foundation, and hardship
Hardship and affliction, the Temple’s foundation, and the promise of blessing
The Temple’s foundation, hardship, and the cancellation of blessing
challenge.explanation: The people are told to compare the hardship before the foundation with the promised blessing from that day onward.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence in the passage?

answers: The blessing is promised even though the crops had not yet produced
The blessing had ended before the foundation was laid
The blessing depended only on the amount of wine
challenge.explanation: The seed was still in the barn and the trees had not yet brought forth, yet the LORD promised to bless them.
challenge.q: What is significant about the promise of blessing?

paragraphs.title: The Shaking of the World’s Kingdoms

answers: Zerubbabel
All the kings of the nations
The priests only
easy.explanation: Haggai was told to speak the second message to Zerubbabel.
easy.q: To whom was the second message of the LORD given?

answers: Only the sea
The heavens and the earth
Only Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will shake the heavens and the earth.”
easy.q: What did the LORD say He would shake?

answers: They would be raised
They would be preserved
They would be overthrown
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms.”
easy.q: What would happen to the thrones of the kingdoms?

answers: To move and greatly disturb
To quiet and calm
To build and strengthen
medium.explanation: The LORD describes a great disturbance of the heavens, earth, and kingdoms.
medium.q: What does “shake” mean in this passage?

answers: Their strength would be destroyed
They would receive new thrones
They would build the Temple
medium.explanation: The LORD said He would destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen.
medium.q: What would happen to the kingdoms of the heathen?

answers: They came down, and the horses and riders fell by the sword of his brother
They arrived in peace
The priests began to ride them
medium.explanation: The passage describes the overthrow of chariots and the fall of horses and their riders.
medium.q: What happened to the chariots and riders?

answers: Shaking, overthrowing kingdoms, destroying their strength, and bringing down chariots and riders
The riders fall, the kingdoms are built, and then the earth shakes
Peace comes, the earth shakes, and the kingdoms grow stronger
challenge.explanation: This is the order of the actions described by the LORD.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the vision?

answers: Only the farmers’ fields
The heavens, the earth, and the governing power of the nations
Only the Temple
challenge.explanation: The shaking includes the heavens and earth, the thrones of kingdoms, and the strength of the nations.
challenge.q: What is the main focus of the shaking in this passage?

answers: All nations entered into peace
The collapse brought conflict between people
The swords immediately disappeared
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes conflict in which people turned against one another.
challenge.q: What does “every one by the sword of his brother” show about the result?

paragraphs.title: Zerubbabel as a Signet and the Promise of Kingship

answers: Zerubbabel
All the priests
All the kings of the nations
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will take thee, O Zerubbabel.”
easy.q: Whom did the LORD say He would take in that day?

answers: As a fortified city
As a signet
As a chariot
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will make thee as a signet.”
easy.q: How did the LORD describe Zerubbabel?

answers: Because He had chosen him
Because he was the high priest
Because he had built every city
easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “For I have chosen thee.”
easy.q: Why did the LORD choose Zerubbabel?

answers: A personal seal kept close by its owner
A large weapon of war
A place for storing grain
medium.explanation: A signet is a personal seal associated closely with its owner.

answers: He was the son of Shealtiel and the LORD’s servant
He was the son of Josedech and the high priest
He was king of Egypt and builder of the Temple
medium.explanation: Zerubbabel is called the son of Shealtiel and the LORD’s servant.
medium.q: Which details about Zerubbabel appear in the verse?

answers: The image emphasizes Zerubbabel’s closeness to and favored position before the LORD
The image proves Zerubbabel would become a merchant
The image describes the fall of the chariots
medium.explanation: The LORD chose Zerubbabel and compared him to a personal signet kept close by its owner.
medium.q: What connection exists between being chosen and being made a signet?

answers: A promise connected with the final and enduring kingship
A promise of a harvest of twenty measures
A promise that all nations would become priests
challenge.explanation: The central idea connects Zerubbabel’s choice with the promise of the final and enduring kingdom.
challenge.q: What broader promise is associated with the LORD’s words about Zerubbabel?

answers: He is called the LORD’s servant and is also said to be chosen by Him
He is called the high priest
He is described as riding a horse
challenge.explanation: The verse includes both “my servant” and “I have chosen thee.”
challenge.q: What detail in the verse about Zerubbabel is easy to overlook?

answers: It follows the shaking of kingdoms by emphasizing the LORD’s choice of Zerubbabel
It cancels the promise of glory for the Temple
It returns only to the question of uncleanness
challenge.explanation: After describing the shaking of kingdoms, the LORD highlights Zerubbabel’s chosen position.
challenge.q: How does this verse connect with the earlier promises in the chapter?
